# Description
*Filip* notebook for calculating LD blocks from GWAS data.

Filips list of files that were downloaded:
gwas-catalog-v1.0.3-ancestries-r2021-07-08.tsv
gwas_catalog_v1.0.2-associations_e104_r2021-07-08.tsv
(not needed?)gwas_catalog_v1.0.2-studies_r2021-07-08.tsv 


15.12. Updating for 2022 gwas catalog release
ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gwas/releases/2022/11/30
gwas-catalog-associations_ontology-annotated.tsv
gwas-catalog-ancestry.tsv
(not needed?)gwas-catalog-studies_ontology-annotated.tsv


In this notebook:
* GWAS data is downloaded and processed to include only european ancestry (to be expanded).
* Next, LDblock for each gwas SNP was calculated with LDlinkR. This step requires a token and queries online databases in order to calculate LDblock. It is a bottleneck since time required is about 2 weeks to calculate SNPs for our GWAS dataset. This part should be prepared on a computing cluster.
* SNP LDblock results are aggregated and an interval is calculated R2>0.6.
* Final object contains GWAS data with respective LDblocks.

# Preprocessing
Before running LDproxy, data preprocessing is required.
In this phase of the project we include only studies on European ancestry participants.
```{r}
# Number of studies based on ancestry 
as.data.frame(table(unique(select(gwas_ancestry, STUDY.ACCESSION, BROAD.ANCESTRAL.CATEGORY))$BROAD.ANCESTRAL.CATEGORY)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Freq))%>%
  head()

# Studies on European ancestries
gwas_ancestry_eu <- gwas_ancestry %>%
  filter(BROAD.ANCESTRAL.CATEGORY == "European")

# Filtering associations of European ancestry
gwas_associations <-
  gwas_associations %>%
  filter(is.element(STUDY.ACCESSION, gwas_ancestry_eu$STUDY.ACCESSION))

```
Preparing SNPs as input for LDproxy.
SNPs in the SNP column that are "x" delimited or ; delimeted are filtered out since thos represent SNP-SNP interactions or multi-SNP haplotypes that we will not analyze in this phase of the research:  

*5. How are SNP-SNP interactions and multi-SNP haplotypes displayed and annotated?*

*For SNP-SNP interactions, all elements that are specific to a given SNP (rsID, risk allele, mapped gene, chromosome location etc) are separated by an "x" (eg "rs1336472-A x rs4715555-G", "1p31.3 x 6p12.1", "3_prime_UTR_variant x upstream_gene_variant"). For multi-SNP haplotypes, elements are separated by a ";" (eg "rs17310467-?; rs6088735-?; rs6060278-?; rs867186-?", "MYH7B; EDEM2 - PROCR; EDEM2 - PROCR; PROCR", "upstream_gene_variant; intergenic_variant; intergenic_variant; missense_variant"). In both cases, the position of each element is the same across all variables, so the first rsID corresponds to the first mapped gene or mapped gene range (for intergenic SNPs), the first bp location etc.*

*While we do provide the mapped gene and position information in this format in both the results page and the download, we excluded some of the additional gene-related information such as upstream/downstream gene IDs and distances from SNPs to genes from the download spreadsheet. This decision was made as it is almost impossible to present this kind of multi-dimensional data cleanly in the current spreadsheet format. In particular in large multi-SNP haplotypes, it is possible for some of the SNPs to be located within a gene while others are intergenic. Splitting gene IDs and distances by in-gene, upstream and downstream position would make the individual values much harder to pair up.*

Furthermore,
* SNPs only with rs ID are selected 
* SNPs without an empty chromosome ID where selected. When querying the GWAS catalog an message pops up: 	
This variant could not be mapped to the genome.

```{r}
# Preparing gwas_snps table
gwas_snps <- gwas_associations %>%
  # Selecting SNP rs ids and chromosomes (used for batch mode LDproxy)
  select(SNPS, CHR_ID) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  # Removing SNP interactions
  filter(!str_detect(SNPS, " x |;")) %>%
  # Selecting only SNPs with rs ID
  filter(str_detect(SNPS, pattern = "^rs")) %>%
  # Removing SNPs that do not have chromosome ID
  filter(str_detect(CHR_ID, pattern = ""))

write.table(gwas_snps$SNPS, file = file.path(project_dir, "data/processed/gwas_snps_2021.txt"), quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
# Spliting gwas_snps df into a list based on chromosomes
gwas_snps_ls <- split(gwas_snps, gwas_snps$CHR_ID) 

saveRDS(gwas_snps_ls, file = file.path(project_dir, "data/processed/2022/gwas_snps_ls.rds"))
```

# LDproxy

Running LD proxy batch mode.
For each query snp per chromosome returns a txt file containing the resulting SNPs with LD metrics. More details on LDlinkR documentation
Since this is a long job it is submitted on Isabella cluster.
Transfer following files to the cluster:
- gwas_snps_ls.rds
- ldproxy_qsub.sge
- ldproxy.R 

### ldproxy job submitting script
First line is necessary and with minimal parameters.
-N is name of the job
-cwd defines that the dir with the starting script is the working directory
ldproxy_qsub.sge
```{}
#!/bin/bash

#$ -N LDproxy
#$ -cwd

module load R
R CMD BATCH ldproxy.R Rcodeoutput.txt
```

### ldproxy R script
LDlinkR library was install previously. The isabella and orthus cluster have an option to install it as a private library. Commands for installing:
**Loading R module** 
module load R
**Running R**
R
install.packages("LDlinkR")

The working directory is set depending on the isabella cluster.
Additionally gwas_snps_ls.rds file is transfered to the cluster which contains list of SNPs used for calculating LD blocks. LDproxy function has a deafult value for the genome assembly as grch37!
ldproxy.R
```{r ldproxy, eval=FALSE}
library(LDlinkR)

wd <- getwd()
gwas_snps_ls <- readRDS(file.path(wd,"gwas_snps_ls.rds"))

ldlink_token <- "be94d998f060"


for(chr in names(gwas_snps_ls)[]){
  

  # Creating a dir for each chromosome
  dir <- file.path(wd,chr)
  dir.create(dir)
  setwd(dir)
  
  # Nested for loop for skipping errors
  for(rs in gwas_snps_ls[[chr]]$SNPS){
    
  # Running LDproxy_batch 
  # tryCatch skips errors that occur because of snps missing from LDproxy databases
  tryCatch(LDproxy_batch(rs, pop = "CEU", r2d = "r2", token = ldlink_token, append = F),
           error=function(e){cat("ERROR :",conditionMessage(e), "\n")})
  }
  
}
```

Script for running LD proxy on a cluster.
```{}
#!/bin/bash

#$ -N LDproxy
#$ -cwd

module load R
R CMD BATCH ldproxy.R Rcodeoutput_ldproxy.txt
```


# LD Aggregation
Collect results for all chromosomes outputted from LDlink.
Aggregate into a table with queried SNP rs ID. 
Separate coord column into chr and range.
**Removing all SNPs with R2 lower than 0.8.** (Older iteration)
*Removing all SNPs with R2 lower than 0.6.*
## ldAggregation script
A script LD_data_aggregation.R is below and it
```{r LD data aggregation, eval=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)

# Path from working dir to LDproxy output dir
LDout_dir <- "data/LDproxy"
#list.dirs(LDout_dir)
gwas_snps_LDblocks <- data.frame()

for(chr in list.dirs(LDout_dir)[2:25]){
  message(chr)
  
  # Path of each queried SNP
  all_paths <- list.files(path = chr, pattern = "*.txt", full.names = T, recursive = T)
  
  # Filenames stored as a list
  all_filenames <- all_paths %>%
    basename() %>%
    as.list()
  
  # Read all output files into a single list of data frames
  all_content <- all_paths %>% 
    lapply(read.table,
           header = TRUE,
           sep = "\t",
           encoding = "UTF-8")
  
  # Append filenames to corresponding df in list of dataframes (filenames = queried SNP for each df)
  all_lists <- mapply(c, all_content, all_filenames, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
  
  # Make a single dataframe from list of dataframes
  all_result <- rbindlist(all_lists, fill = T)
  
  # Separate filename to remove .txt extension, remove unnecessary columns, separate coord column into chromosome number and loc (locus coordinates on chromosome), keep only SNPs correlated with the query snp with R2 > 0.8 
  all_results_0.6 <- separate(all_result, V1, c('query_snp', 'rest'), "[.]") %>%
    select(-rest, -Function) %>%
    separate(Coord, c('chromosome', 'loc'), ':') %>%
    transform(loc = as.numeric(loc)) %>%
    as.data.frame(all_results) %>% 
    filter(R2 >= 0.6)
  
  
  all_results_0.6_chr <- select(all_results_0.6, query_snp, chromosome) %>%
    unique()
  
  # Get LD Block range
  # Get table with start and end coordinates for LD block of queried SNP
  range_table <- all_results_0.6 %>% 
    group_by(query_snp) %>% 
    summarize(max_loc = max(loc), min_loc = min(loc)) %>%
    left_join(all_results_0.6_chr)
  
  # gwas_snps_LDblocks <- rbind(gwas_snps_LDblocks, range_table)
}

saveRDS(gwas_snps_LDblocks, file="gwas_snps_LDblocks.rds")
```

# LDproxy failed SNPs
some SNPs fail the pipeline (either missing chromosome ID, or rejected by LDproxy), list the failures for further analysis. 
To run this scrpit transfer: 
gwas_snps_ls.rds (stored in LDproxy_failedSNP dir)
ldproxy.R
failedSnps_qsub.sge
to a sge runned cluster and run the job 

Run this chunk locally to extract the faileds SNPs
```{r, eval=FALSE}
# After finishing the scripts on the cluster transfer the resulting rds locally
gwas_snps_LDblocks <- readRDS("data/gwas_snps_LDblocks.rds") %>%
  # Removing "_grch37" from the query snp name
  mutate(SNPS = str_split(query_snp, pattern = "_", simplify = TRUE)[,1]) %>%
  # Creating a column for LDblock that can be easily converted to gr 
  # Format: chr1:1234-1456
  mutate(LDblock = str_c(chromosome,":",min_loc,"-",max_loc)) %>%
  dplyr::select(SNPS, LDblock)

# Determining failed SNPs
failed_snps <- gwas_snps %>%
  filter(!is.element(SNPS, gwas_snps_LDblocks$SNPS))

  #setdiff(pull(gwas_snps, SNPS), pull(gwas_snps_LDblocks, SNPS))
# Do not need the list atm
#failed_snps_ls <- split(failed_snps, failed_snps$CHR_ID)

saveRDS(failed_snps, "data/gwas_failed_snps.rds")
```
